meaning: Candidate earliest useful processing age, NOT worldgen/harvest gating. A mineral marked conditional does not unlock until its prerequisite consumer/process exists. Deferred minerals have no assigned unlock age.
mining_policy: All registered ore blocks retain current self-drops and stone-tool mining baseline. An inactive mineral can be found/mined; do not gate critical early ore behind a later tool.
compatibility_policy: No registered ore IDs, worldgen, loot, crafting recipes, JEI rules or existing Copper/Bronze production yields are changed by this planning matrix. Preserve legacy silicium/platinium IDs.
quality_policy: Preserve vanilla-versus-mod Copper quality decisions. No new grade math, NBT migration, or recipe yield changes without an explicit later implementation.
gating_rules: Technology: machines available in the age must plausibly carry out the process.
Gameplay: a resulting material must have a named and useful consumer.
Progression: early availability must not bypass a later milestone.
No dead ends: no isolated concentrate or ingot recipe merely to populate an age.

ages.purpose: No mandatory ore-specific processing; vanilla clay and ordinary fuels already cover the first technologies.
Preserve proven Copper, Tin and Quartz recipes and material quality conventions.
Magnetite is the K1 iron-bloom baseline; Hematite/Limonite require demonstrably distinct preparation and downstream Bloomery use.
Candidate carbon/lubrication, high-grade fuel and brass processing only if consumers exist.
Candidate alloying and industrial abrasion, gated by actual Steel production.
Sulfur chemistry only if a named industrial chemical consumer exists.
Petroleum extraction/refining is not a mandatory mineral-ore unlock.
Electrical contacts, specialty metal reduction and aluminum electrolysis require functioning electric technology.
Real uranium fuel cycle rather than a symbolic ore smelting recipe.

chalcocite.prerequisites: Preserve the Grinder, Washer, Sifter and Primitive Furnace 1/2/3-copper yield tiers; the Roasting Kiln is a separate optional improvement.
chalcocite.rationale: An established required Copper material and existing recipes.

cassiterite.prerequisites: Preserve existing copper-to-bronze tin chain, including processing water and slag accounting.
cassiterite.rationale: Tin is required for Bronze production.

quartz.prerequisites: Preserve existing crushing, washing and sifting; later silicon chemistry must not erase the current route.
quartz.rationale: Already processed and useful, with later possibilities that do not force an early electronics path.

magnetite.first_use: Iron Bloom from the existing Bloomery
magnetite.prerequisites: Existing Stamp Mill → Washer → Sifter → concentrate; Calcite flux, charcoal, HEAT and real AIR are mandatory. Wrought Iron consolidation is still missing.
magnetite.rationale: First actual Bronze-to-Iron reduction route exists in source; user has formed and used the Bloomery, but the full survival chain is not yet accepted.

hematite.prerequisites: Approve an ore-specific concentration method and compare its yield and availability with Magnetite. Use the same Bloomery only when mechanically justified.
hematite.rationale: Second iron-oxide source can provide exploration variety; it must not require a duplicate machine or dead-end concentrate.

limonite.first_use: Alternative iron-bloom feed after drying/roasting when beneficial
limonite.prerequisites: Prove the hydrated iron-bearing feed benefits from existing drying or Ore Roasting Kiln, and provide a real Bloomery recipe.
limonite.rationale: Would give the existing kiln a material-specific role; no universal roasting tax.

graphite.prerequisites: Only unlock with a named Iron-era bearing, hot-working, crucible or heat-resistant component that consumes it.
graphite.rationale: Graphite should not become a purposeless coal replacement.

anthracite.prerequisites: Define a measurable difference in heat/cleanliness/duration from charcoal and coal in a machine that needs it.
anthracite.rationale: A valuable industrial fuel only if machines benefit from its characteristics.

sphalerite.first_use: Zinc feedstock for useful brass components
sphalerite.prerequisites: Add a proper zinc extraction route, identify brass consumers and prevent ordinary furnace ore-to-brass shortcuts.
sphalerite.rationale: Brass fittings or precision parts may make zinc meaningful in Iron technology.

manganese.prerequisites: Require an actual alloy/furnace recipe with improved or distinct steel-component use.
manganese.rationale: Useful for alloy design, not simply an extra decorative ingot.

garnierite.prerequisites: Only use after nickel metallurgy and a named alloy or corrosion-resistant component are designed.
garnierite.rationale: Nickel steels are an appropriate eventual Steel-era upgrade if the heat/process requirements are supported.

kimberlite.first_use: Industrial diamond recovery for durable cutting/abrasive tools
kimberlite.prerequisites: Define recovery yields and a genuinely wear-resistant cutting/grinding tool; never convert all Kimberlite directly into diamonds.
kimberlite.rationale: A rock hosting diamonds, rather than a steel alloy ore; toolmaking gives a relevant purpose.

sulfur.prerequisites: Require a specific Steam-era chemical product and machine consumer, such as controlled acid processing or elastomer treatment; not a bare Furnace recipe.
sulfur.rationale: Plausible bulk chemical feed when chemical processing becomes an actual system.

silver.first_use: Electrical contacts or specialist conductive parts
silver.prerequisites: Only unlock with an actual electrical component; preserve vanilla materials compatibility and do not force Silver into basic iron forging.
silver.rationale: No necessary Iron-era consumer currently exists; its most credible planned utility is electrical.

chromite.prerequisites: Define a sufficiently advanced reduction process and actual corrosion-resistant component; revisit Steel placement only if its furnaces legitimately support it.
chromite.rationale: Chromium alloy extraction is too demanding to assume ordinary Steel-era smelting suffices.

bauxite.prerequisites: Require real electrically powered aluminum extraction and meaningful aluminum components.
bauxite.rationale: Energy-intensive refining makes this a natural electric milestone.

cryolite.prerequisites: Link explicitly to Bauxite refining; allow a carefully balanced non-ore supply alternative if necessary to prevent mining bottlenecks.
cryolite.rationale: Not an independently smeltable metal; useful only together with aluminum production.

wolframite.first_use: Tungsten feed for cutting tools or high-temperature components
wolframite.prerequisites: Require appropriate advanced reduction and useful wear-resistant, heat-resistant tooling.
wolframite.rationale: More credible after high-temperature electric metallurgy than as free Steel Age tungsten.

tantalite.prerequisites: Require an electronics/capacitor consumer and a realistic specialty-metal process.
tantalite.rationale: Electric/advanced electronics provides a distinct demand.

cobaltite.prerequisites: Require a named advanced alloy, component or chemical consumer; avoid direct ore-to-pure-cobalt recipes.
cobaltite.rationale: This ore matters only if advanced manufacture uses cobalt.

platinium.prerequisites: Require a named catalyst or specialist component; retain existing registry spelling for compatibility.
platinium.rationale: Plausible advanced material, not a generic Bronze-age precious metal.

uraninite.first_use: Uranium-bearing feed for nuclear fuel fabrication
uraninite.prerequisites: Require a dedicated fuel cycle, radiation containment and actual reactor consumption; no furnace-to-fuel-rod shortcut.
uraninite.rationale: The nuclear age has an obvious genuine consumer but the process is not implemented.

kaolinite.prerequisites: Revisit if kaolin ceramics add a meaningful upgrade over existing clay/sand and fired refractory production.
kaolinite.rationale: A Stone-age ceramic recipe would currently duplicate established inputs without adding gameplay.

lignite.prerequisites: Revisit only if low-grade coal provides an actual resource/combustion tradeoff; never replace mandatory charcoal in the Bloomery.
lignite.rationale: Stone/Copper already have usable fuels; a redundant low-efficiency fuel is not necessary.

galena.prerequisites: Revisit in later metalworking or chemical/electric production when lead or associated silver has a named sink.
galena.rationale: A plausible Bronze extraction process is not sufficient reason to add dead-end Lead Ingots.

saltpeter.prerequisites: Revisit alongside a later fertilizer or controlled industrial chemical chain.
saltpeter.rationale: Do not introduce a chemical ore because Steam Age has a chemistry label.

apatite.prerequisites: Revisit when agriculture, fertilizer or specialty chemical production creates meaningful demand.
apatite.rationale: An early phosphate concentrate would currently be a dead-end item.

cinnabar.prerequisites: Only reconsider with a distinct, justified process that accounts for hazardous mercury chemistry; do not make it a mandatory age gate.
cinnabar.rationale: No need to add Mercury extraction just because the ore exists.

silicium.first_use: Existing legacy mineral ID has no coherent product definition
silicium.prerequisites: Design Silicon production from the existing Quartz/silica path first; decide what silicium_ore represents without renaming saved-world IDs.
silicium.rationale: Native elemental Silicon ore is not a credible natural source; existing Quartz already supplies silica.

titanite.first_use: No approved titanium consumer or practical feed process
titanite.prerequisites: Only reconsider if an advanced titanium route has credible chemistry and useful outputs; do not treat Titanite as simple raw titanium.
titanite.rationale: Titanite is not an easy high-grade titanium ore and should not be mandatory solely to populate Electric Age.

osmiridium.prerequisites: Define a distinct endgame use and appropriate processing before assigning it to Nuclear or an earlier age.
osmiridium.rationale: Its legacy endgame ore status is not in itself a reason for a recipe.
